file name: azure-identity-1.18.5.jar Suppressed as this is an Azure SDK dependency, not application insights.
CVE-2023-36415 (fixed in azure-identity 1.10.0) and CVE-2024-35255 (fixed in azure-identity 1.12.2) are false positives here: the project resolves com.azure:azure-identity:1.18.5, well above the vulnerable ranges for either CVE.

CVE-2026-33117 is reported against an Azure SDK transitive dependency.
The CVE affects the Java Key Vault Keys library's local cryptographic verification path. This application does not include com.azure:azure-security-keyvault-keys and does not use the affected local cryptographic verification path.
This SHA-1 identifies the exact azure-core-http-netty JAR resolved by this application. The suppression is intentionally scoped to this artifact and should be reviewed if the dependency version changes.

file name: msal4j-1.23.1.jar CVE-2024-35255 (Azure Identity / MSAL elevation of privilege) affects com.microsoft.azure:msal4j versions >= 1.14.4-beta and < 1.15.1, fixed in 1.15.1. This project resolves com.microsoft.azure:msal4j:1.23.1 (pulled in transitively via com.azure:azure-identity:1.18.5), well above the vulnerable range. False positive.

DOMPurify vulnerabilities detected via the RetireJS analyzer against the DOMPurify build bundled inside vendored Swagger UI JS assets.
Two jars carry a copy of this bundled DOMPurify: - org.wiremock:wiremock-standalone:3.13.2 (swagger-ui-bundle.js / swagger-ui-es-bundle.js) WireMock is a development/test dependency, not included in the production application runtime, and its Swagger UI is not exposed in production. - org.webjars:swagger-ui:5.32.11 (pulled in transitively by springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui:3.1.0), which IS served in production by this API. Forcing a newer org.webjars:swagger-ui version via a Gradle dependency constraint was attempted but breaks springdoc's resource resolution for /swagger-ui/index.html (springdoc 3.1.0 hardcodes swagger-ui 5.32.11 internally), so an in-place version bump is not currently viable. Accepted as risk pending a springdoc-openapi upgrade that bundles a patched swagger-ui/DOMPurify version.
A sha1-based suppression was tried first but does not reliably match: RetireJS reports findings against the individual bundled .js file (whose sha1 changes with the exact bundling), not the containing jar's sha1, and the DOMPurify CVE/GHSA set keeps growing as GitHub backfills additional advisories for the same underlying issue. Matching on the DOMPurify packageUrl (as dps-gradle-spring-boot-suppressions.xml, generated by the hmpps-gradle-spring-boot plugin, already does for older DOMPurify CVEs) is the reliable approach. The packageUrl is scoped to only the two DOMPurify versions actually detected in this project's bundled Swagger UI assets (3.2.6 in wiremock-standalone, 3.4.12 in org.webjars:swagger-ui) rather than a wildcard match, so a future real DOMPurify dependency (a different version) would not be silently suppressed.
CVE-2026-75838 affects DOMPurify versions before 3.4.13 and is therefore applicable to the bundled 3.4.12 copy. The finding is accepted for the same reasons above: the affected copy is bundled in Swagger UI rather than resolved as an independent Gradle dependency, and the WireMock copy is test-only and not exposed in production. Remediation remains pending an upstream artifact containing DOMPurify >= 3.4.13.
